title: Axial-flux motor
summary: Hand-wound copper, printed mechanics and a real lab test.
work: Designed, wound and assembled an axial-flux motor; the photographs show nine coils and a common-axis rotor assembly.
The workshop crank generator and LED heart explain energy transfer through an interactive illustration.
limits: No motor rating or measured efficiency is inferred. The generator and LED heart are explanatory exhibit additions.

title: Three-axis camera gimbal
summary: Printed brackets, hobby servos and a phone-based sensing workaround.
work: Three nested servo axes support a payload; the mechanical design was adapted from an internet design.
The project used a phone gyro workaround after an MPU sensor problem. The compared datasets were not synchronized.
The exhibit demonstrates ideal counter-rotation, rather than reproducing the original firmware or measured control performance.
limits: No validated PID accuracy or unlimited physical servo travel. The full-turn sliders are exhibit orientations.
credit: Student mechatronics project; adapted mechanical design, original creator not identified in available evidence.

title: Battery management system
summary: Physical instrumentation and PCB work alongside switched-capacitor balancing simulation.
work: EE401 planned the system; EE402 documented the outcomes, instrumentation and prototype.
The balancing model moves charge using a switched capacitor. This simulation is distinct from the photographed physical hardware.
Visitors change individual cells, load and temperature to explore balancing and thermal load cutoff.
limits: Long-term hardware balancing and protection validation was unfinished. Displayed values and accelerated time are illustrative.
credit: Senior-year team project; shared hardware and simulation evidence.

title: Boundary-scanning Zumo robot
summary: Reflectance sensing, IR scans and a maximum count across repeated trials.
work: Calibrate reflectance sensors, move toward the white edge while avoiding IR detections, then scan and return.
Store counts from ten trials and signal the maximum through the LED and buzzer.
Five illustrated arrangements succeeded; one arrangement at the boundary failed.
limits: No SLAM, object-identity map or statistical accuracy claim. Repeated IR detections can count the same object. This geometric exhibit simplifies traction, timing and sensor optics.
credit: Yunus Emre Ozan and Seyit Kubilay Uluçay. Uses Pololu Zumo libraries.

title: Power flow & economic dispatch
summary: A MATLAB App Designer interface for an educational network and generator cost model.
work: Two modes expose power flow and economic dispatch with three generators.
The dispatch callback solves equal marginal-cost equations with a demand constraint, then calculates quadratic costs.
The source includes fixed network coefficients and UI controls for generator settings.
limits: Static source review only; the MATLAB runtime and solver were not validated here. Not an operational grid planning tool; feasibility limits need separate checking.
credit: Named individual MATLAB submission by Kubilay Uluçay.

title: Off-grid residential PV design
summary: A PVsyst sizing and feasibility study for a house in Kocaeli.
work: The source report proposes eight 580 W modules (4.64 kW) and approximately 38.3 kWh stored energy.
Weather, load, storage and winter availability drive the simulation trade-offs.
The financial analysis uses May 2025 assumptions and finds poor simple payback, around 62 years.
limits: Simulated proposal, not an installed system. Historical component prices and payback are not current recommendations.
credit: Seyit Kubilay Uluçay and Mehmet Fatih Karaosman.

title: Wind-farm interconnection trade-offs
summary: Compare conductor and substation choices across 27 educational model configurations.
work: PowerWorld cases compare cost, loss and overload constraints for a hypothetical 200 MW wind-farm connection.
The analysis narrows feasible configurations instead of assuming the lowest-loss case is automatically best.
limits: A classroom network study, not a built wind farm or a commercial engineering recommendation.

title: Tweets & market-direction classification
summary: BERT embeddings feed an MLP classifier for daily grouped tweets.
work: After filtering and daily grouping, the report uses 219 examples.
The pipeline compares MLP hyperparameters using BERT-transformed text.
The report describes failed imputation attempts before changing the research question.
limits: Random train/test splitting and test-set tuning limit the reported score. No causal influence, reliable trading return or deployable forecast is established. BERT, not BART.
credit: Seyit Kubilay Uluçay and Emir Arda Gün.

title: PLC sequences: traffic lights & toy claw
summary: Two Control Expert PLC/HMI exercises: timed traffic-light modes and a staged claw game.
work: Traffic-light logic models normal and after-hours modes with HMI controls.
The claw game uses a coin input, a 90-second positioning window and a staged gripper sequence.
The shared team report documents both scenarios and the issues encountered during testing.
limits: Academic simulation; no roadside deployment or physical claw-machine build is confirmed. Peer-only Lab3 and provided solution files are excluded.
credit: Berke Çeçen, Efe Can Özhan, Genco Güven and Kubilay Uluçay.

title: Circuits, op-amps & transients
summary: Six EE202 reports connect network laws and op-amp behavior with RC/555 timing and RL/LC response.
work: Lab01 covers KCL/KVL resistor networks; Lab02 compares network equivalents and superposition.
Lab03 examines op-amp input/output and gain; Lab04 studies integrators and differentiators.
Lab05 investigates RC response and LM555 timing; Lab06 documents inductor construction and RL/LC response.
limits: Original course observations and calculations are not independently recertified. Identifying cover pages are omitted; Lab04 is split into two consecutive layout-preserving parts under the hosting file-size limit.
credit: Original EE202 reports by Seyit Kubilay Uluçay, March–May 2023.

title: Diodes, transistors & LTspice
summary: Four EE301 reports compare diode, BJT, MOSFET and amplifier behavior with LTspice and lab observations.
work: Lab01 covers DC analysis and diode I–V behavior; Lab03 examines BJT characteristics and current gain.
Lab04 records MOSFET bias and drain-current measurements; Lab05 documents amplifiers, an unsuccessful NMOS bench result and unfinished work.
limits: Original observations are not independently recertified. Identifying covers are omitted. The Lab02 brief is not a student report, and native LTspice files are absent from this reviewed set.
credit: Original EE301 reports by Seyit Kubilay Uluçay, Fall 2023.

title: Sensors, timing & motor feedback
summary: Nine ME417 reports connect analog sensing, timing, I²C and motor drive with encoder feedback.
work: Bench and Arduino I/O, analog measurement, CNY70 sensing, switching, NE555 timing and button debouncing form the early reports.
Op-amp gain, a two-Arduino I²C link, Hall encoder signals and L298N/PWM drive lead into motor-position tests.
The encoder report includes an interrupt-counting excerpt. The later report records proportional-control tests but says the full PID modification could not be tested.
limits: Full PID testing was prevented by a serial-plotter problem. Encoder timing and scale factors are not independent mechanical-speed calibration. Identifying cover pages are omitted from public reports.
credit: Original ME417 reports by Seyit Kubilay Uluçay, March–May 2024.

title: Signals & LabVIEW communications
summary: Five team submissions connect Fourier displays, sampled audio and DSB-SC work, with selected LabVIEW VIs.
work: Named Section C Team 1 submissions cover Fourier/FFT displays, sampling, audio synchronization and DSB-SC preparation/transmission.
Eleven native VIs are preserved from the selected team archives. Identical Lab 3 pre-lab/in-lab archives are counted once.
A saved MATLAB modulation-comparison plot is credited separately to the Uluçay–İlkbahar bonus pair.
limits: Peer-labelled and unverified work is excluded. No new VI/MATLAB/USRP execution or performance validation is claimed. Native files may need LabVIEW/course dependencies; reports include provided task text and shared scaffolding.
credit: Section C Team 1: Seyit Kubilay Uluçay, Ali Umut İlkbahar, Kaan Şekerci and Ahmet Genco Güven; bonus output: Uluçay and İlkbahar.

title: Java programming & OOP exercises
summary: Named Java exercises alongside object-oriented programming practice.
work: Student exercise files and authored-work folders support programming coursework.
Grouped as coursework rather than presenting each small exercise as a standalone product.
One inspected exercise reads N, generates a random x and accumulates a factorial-weighted series; this small exercise is not itself an OOP application.
limits: Provided answers, exams and empty assignment folders do not establish completed student projects. No application deployment is claimed.
credit: Kubilay Uluçay coursework; supplied solutions excluded.

title: Deforestation research presentation
summary: Research synthesis and visual communication about deforestation.
work: A classroom presentation assembles environmental research into a structured argument.
limits: Literature-based communication, not field research or an implemented conservation programme.
credit: Student research presentation; cited research remains credited to its authors.

title: EcoRevive / ReLifeTech pitch
summary: A team pitch for extending the useful life of discarded electronics.
work: The presentation proposes collecting and repairing devices for reuse, including alternative device roles.
Persuasive speaking and proposal structure were the learning goals.
limits: Hypothetical classroom venture. No Samsung partnership, funding, operating company or achieved environmental metrics are claimed.
credit: Seyit Kubilay Uluçay, Ahmet Emre İpek, Berke Çeçen, Efe Can Özhan and Genco Güven.

title: Floor sensing in an R&D team
summary: Public-safe context for sensor integration, data analysis and test documentation.
work: Worked within an R&D team on sensing for robot-vacuum floor detection.
Contributed to sensor integration, test observations, data analysis and documentation.
limits: Client/internal designs and metrics are omitted. Team involvement does not imply patent inventorship or sole ownership.
credit: Internship contribution within Beko R&D Advanced Sensor Technologies.
